어른.x: You should use polite speech with elders.
어른.e: Also 'elder' — showing respect to 어른 is a big part of Korean manners.

계절.e: Both parts mean 'season'. 사계절 = the four seasons.
계절.t: Often pronounced [게절]: ㅖ after a consonant usually sounds like ㅔ.

앞.x: Let's meet in front of the school.
앞.e: 학교 앞 = in front of the school. 앞으로 = from now on.

파티.x: There's a friend's birthday party on Saturday.

다이어트.x: I started dieting before summer came.
다이어트.e: From English 'diet'; in Korean it almost always means dieting to lose weight.

배드민턴.x: Every weekend I play badminton with my dad in the park.
배드민턴.t: Racket and ball-hitting sports use 치다: 배드민턴을 치다, 테니스를 치다, 탁구를 치다.

점심시간.ex: 점심시간에 회사 근처 식당에서 비빔밥을 먹었어요.
점심시간.x: I ate bibimbap at a restaurant near the office during lunch break.
점심시간.e: 점심 literally 'a dot on the heart' — a light snack to tide you over.

조카.ex: 언니의 아들인 조카가 올해 초등학생이 됐어요.
조카.x: My nephew, my sister's son, started elementary school this year.
조카.e: One word for both nephew and niece; 조카딸 specifies a niece.

물론.forms: 물론이에요 = Of course; 물론 A지만 B = A, of course, but B
물론.x: Of course I'm going to the party too.
물론.e: Literally 'no need to discuss' — so obvious it goes without saying.

처럼.forms: Same form after any noun, with or without batchim: 꽃처럼, 학생처럼
처럼.x: My younger sibling sings as well as a singer.
처럼.t: N처럼 and N같이 are interchangeable: 꽃처럼 = 꽃같이 'like a flower'.
rel: to be the same, be like

순대.x: At the tteokbokki place, we ordered sundae too.
순대.e: Word of uncertain origin (one theory links it to a Manchu word for blood sausage). It's pig intestine stuffed with glass noodles and pork blood, then steamed.
순대.t: Not the ice-cream sundae! 떡튀순 (떡볶이 + 튀김 + 순대) is the classic snack-bar combo.

네모.ex: 저는 동그란 접시보다 네모 접시가 좋아요.
네모.x: I like square plates better than round ones.
네모.e: Native: 네 'four' + 모 'corner, edge'. Likewise 세모 'triangle' (세 'three').
네모.t: The adjective is 네모나다: 네모난 상자 'a square box'. Everyday 네모 covers squares and rectangles alike; 정사각형 and 직사각형 are the math terms.

사원.ex: 우리 회사는 올해 신입 사원을 열 명 뽑았어요.
사원.x: Our company hired ten new employees this year.
사원.e: Literally 'company member'. A homonym 사원 (different hanja) means 'temple'.

조건.ex: 이 집은 위치와 가격 조건이 모두 좋아요.
조건.x: This place is good on both location and price.
조건.e: Literally 'clause and item,' like terms listed in a contract.

실천하다.m: to put into practice, to act on
실천하다.ex: 환경을 위해 작은 일부터 실천해 보세요.
실천하다.x: Try putting small things into practice for the environment.
실천하다.e: Literally 'actually tread': turning words into action.

변비.x: Drinking a lot of water helps with constipation.

지연되다.ex: 폭설 때문에 비행기 출발이 두 시간 지연됐습니다.
지연되다.x: Because of the heavy snow, the flight's departure was delayed by two hours.

거부하다.m: to refuse, to reject, to deny
거부하다.t: 거부하다 is stronger and more formal than 거절하다, which is a polite 'no' to an offer.

살인.ex: 그 영화는 형사가 살인 사건을 해결하는 이야기예요.
살인.x: That movie is about a detective solving a murder case.

제대.ex: 형은 작년에 제대하고 다시 대학교에 다니고 있어요.
제대.x: My older brother was discharged last year and is back in college.
제대.t: In official settings 전역 is preferred, but 제대 is very common in everyday speech.

면세.x: I bought cosmetics at the airport duty-free shop.

수동적.ex: 수업 시간에 너무 수동적인 태도는 좋지 않아요.
수동적.x: Being too passive in class isn't a good attitude.
수동적.e: Literally 'receiving movement' — being moved by others.

각양각색.ex: 축제에는 각양각색의 옷을 입은 사람들이 있었어요.
각양각색.x: At the festival, there were people wearing all kinds of outfits.
각양각색.e: Literally 'each a different shape, each a different color'.

천차만별.x: Even for the same item, prices vary widely from store to store.
천차만별.e: Literally 'a thousand differences, ten thousand distinctions'.

현안.ex: 정부는 오늘 경제 현안에 대해 논의했습니다.
현안.x: The government discussed pressing economic issues today.
현안.e: Literally 'hanging matter': an issue still up in the air.
현안.t: Pronounced [혀난]; mostly a news and politics word.

심판.x: At the end of the game, the referee called a foul.

세면도구.ex: 호텔에 세면도구가 없어서 챙겨 가야 해요.
세면도구.x: The hotel doesn't provide toiletries, so I have to bring my own.
세면도구.e: Literally 'wash-face tools': toothbrush, toothpaste, soap and so on.
세면도구.t: Since 2024, larger Korean hotels may no longer give out free single-use toiletries, so it's wise to pack your own.

부결되다.m: to be rejected, to be voted down
부결되다.x: The bill was voted down because there weren't enough yes votes.

재원.ex: 복지 정책을 위한 재원을 마련해야 합니다.
재원.x: We need to secure funding for welfare policies.
재원.e: Literally 'wealth source'; a homonym 재원 means a talented person.
재원.t: Collocations: 재원을 마련하다 or 재원을 확보하다 = to secure funding.

패소.ex: 회사는 소송에서 패소해서 손해 배상을 해야 해요.
패소.x: The company lost the lawsuit and has to pay damages.

패권.ex: 두 강대국이 아시아의 패권을 놓고 경쟁하고 있습니다.
패권.x: The two superpowers are competing for dominance in Asia.
패권.e: Literally 'overlord's power' — the top ruler over rival states.
패권.t: Pronounced [패꿘]; also used in sports: 패권을 차지하다 'to win the championship'.

고스란히.m: intact, entirely, just as it was
고스란히.ex: 할머니의 물건이 방에 고스란히 남아 있어요.
고스란히.x: Grandma's things remain in her room exactly as they were.
고스란히.t: Also used for burdens passed on: 피해가 고스란히 국민에게 돌아갔다 'citizens bore all the damage'.

자포자기.x: Don't give up on yourself just because you failed once.

부연하다.m: to elaborate, to expand on, to explain further
부연하다.ex: 제 의견에 대해 조금 더 부연하겠습니다.
부연하다.x: Let me elaborate a little more on my opinion.

곱씹다.m: to chew over, to dwell on, to mull over; to chew repeatedly
곱씹다.ex: 그는 친구가 한 말을 밤새 곱씹었어요.
곱씹다.x: He dwelled on what his friend had said all night.
곱씹다.e: 곱- 'double, again' (as in 곱절) + 씹다 'to chew'.
곱씹다.t: Often used for dwelling on hurtful words or mistakes, while 되새기다 is more neutral or positive.
rel: to go over in one's mind

위안.ex: 음악은 힘든 시기에 저에게 큰 위안이 되었어요.
위안.x: Music was a great comfort to me during hard times.
위안.t: Key patterns: 위안이 되다 (be a comfort), 위안을 얻다 (find comfort), 위안으로 삼다 (take comfort in).

공업화.x: Korea industrialized rapidly from the 1960s on.
공업화.e: Literally 'becoming industrial'; 공업 means manufacturing industry.
공업화.t: Pronounced [공어퐈]; 공업화 and 산업화 are near synonyms, but 산업화 is more common today.

점층법.ex: 점층법은 뜻을 점점 크고 강하게 표현하는 방법이에요.
점층법.x: Climax is a way of expressing meaning in gradually bigger, stronger steps.
점층법.e: Literally 'gradual-layer method' — ideas build up step by step.

소조.ex: 소조는 흙을 붙여 가며 형태를 만드는 기법이에요.
소조.x: Modeling is a technique of building up a form by adding clay.
소조.e: Literally 'molding and making' — building form up, the opposite of carving.
소조.t: 소조 adds material and 조각 carves it away; together they make up 조소 'sculpture.'

도예.ex: 요즘 취미로 도예 수업을 듣고 있어요.
도예.x: These days I'm taking a pottery class as a hobby.

남부여대.m: wandering as refugees with all one's belongings
남부여대.ex: 전쟁이 나자 사람들은 남부여대하여 피난을 떠났어요.
남부여대.x: When war broke out, people fled carrying everything they owned.
남부여대.e: Literally 'men carry on their backs, women on their heads.'

준거하다.m: to be based on, to conform to (a standard)
준거하다.ex: 이 평가는 국제 기준에 준거하여 실시됩니다.
준거하다.x: This assessment is conducted based on international standards.
준거하다.e: Literally 'follow and rely on' a standard.

단언하다.m: to assert, to state flatly, to declare with certainty
단언하다.ex: 그 계획이 성공할 거라고 단언하기는 어려워요.
단언하다.x: It's hard to say for certain that the plan will succeed.
단언하다.e: Literally 'decisive words' — saying it with full certainty.
단언하다.t: Often negative: -다고 단언할 수 없다 'one can't say for sure that ...'.

점유하다.m: to occupy, to hold, to possess
점유하다.ex: 그 회사가 국내 시장의 절반을 점유하고 있어요.
점유하다.x: That company holds half of the domestic market.
점유하다.t: 시장 점유율 'market share' is the phrase you'll see most.

난해하다.ex: 이 철학책은 너무 난해해서 읽기 힘들어요.
난해하다.x: This philosophy book is so abstruse that it's hard to read.

여실하다.ex: 그 소설에는 전쟁의 참상이 여실하게 그려져 있어요.
여실하다.x: That novel depicts the horrors of war true to life.
여실하다.t: Mostly as the adverb 여실히 with 드러나다 or 보여 주다 'to show plainly'.

천연덕스럽다.m: nonchalant, poker-faced, acting perfectly natural (as if nothing happened)
천연덕스럽다.x: Even after lying, he smiled as if nothing had happened.
천연덕스럽다.e: Built on 천연 'natural': acting as natural as can be.
천연덕스럽다.t: Usually after a lie or mischief: 천연덕스럽게 시치미를 떼다 'to play innocent with a straight face'.

취약계층.ex: 폭염 때는 취약계층을 위한 무더위 쉼터가 운영됩니다.
취약계층.x: During heat waves, cooling shelters are run for vulnerable people.

파탄나다.m: to collapse, to break down, to go bankrupt (finances, marriage)
파탄나다.x: Reckless investments caused the company's finances to collapse.
파탄나다.e: Literally 'break and split at the seams' plus native 나다 'to happen'.
파탄나다.t: Also spelled 파탄 나다 with a space; 파탄에 이르다 is a more formal alternative.

패러다임.ex: 인터넷은 사람들이 소통하는 방식의 패러다임을 완전히 바꿨어요.
패러다임.x: The internet completely changed the paradigm of how people communicate.

만고불변.ex: 정직이 최고의 미덕이라는 것은 만고불변의 진리입니다.
만고불변.x: That honesty is the greatest virtue is an eternal truth.
만고불변.t: Almost always in 만고불변의 진리 'an eternal truth'.
